title: Checkpoint: Rails, Factories, Newcomers
objective: After this level you can explain how industry, immigration and the conquest of the West remade the country between 1865 and 1920.
summary: By 1920, for the first time, most Americans lived in urban areas. A timeline from Promontory Summit to the 19th Amendment ties together the rails, factories and newcomers, and who paid the price.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 finale: by 1920, most Americans lived in urban areas.
cards.body: Rails, factories and newcomers got them there, and the West’s first nations paid a heavy price. Let’s put the chapter on one timeline.

cards.headline: From Promontory Summit to the ballot box

events.label: The Dawes Act breaks up reservation land
The 7th Cavalry kills Lakota at Wounded Knee
Tennessee completes ratification of the 19th Amendment

cards.headline: New wealth, new wounds
cards.body: Chinese immigrants built most of the Central Pacific, then the Chinese Exclusion Act shut out Chinese laborers. The Dawes Act took most of the land the Plains wars had left Native nations. Immigrant women sewed behind locked doors until the Triangle fire forced new laws. And the people on the losing end didn’t wait: they struck, sued, wrote and picketed, from Clara Lemlich to Homer Plessy, Ida B. Wells and Alice Paul.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 complete
learned: How railroads, factories and immigrants turned the US into a mostly urban nation by 1920.
Why the Plains nations lost the bison, the Black Hills and most of their remaining land.
What Carnegie, Rockefeller, strikers and muckrakers show about the new industrial economy.
How Plessy, Chinese exclusion and the 19th Amendment drew and redrew who belonged.

questions.prompt: Rails, Factories, Newcomers: which order of events is right?

options.label: Plessy v. Ferguson, the railroad is completed, the 19th Amendment
The railroad is completed, Plessy v. Ferguson, the 19th Amendment
The 19th Amendment, the railroad is completed, Plessy v. Ferguson
The railroad is completed, the 19th Amendment, Plessy v. Ferguson

questions.explanation: The railroad was completed in 1869, Plessy came in 1896 and the 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920.

questions.prompt: What did the 1920 census show for the first time?

options.label: Most Americans were immigrants
Most Americans worked on farms
options.rationale: That was the older pattern, now reversed.

options.label: Most Americans lived in urban areas
Most Americans lived west of the Mississippi

questions.explanation: The 1920 census was the first in which most Americans lived in urban areas.

questions.prompt: How did Native nations lose most of the land they still held after the Plains wars?

options.label: Allotment split reservations and sold the “surplus” to settlers
They sold it to railroads for cash and company stock
options.rationale: The level describes allotment, not railroad sales.

options.label: The Homestead Act banned Native people from owning land
options.rationale: The level makes no such claim.

options.label: Congress moved every Plains nation north into Canada

questions.explanation: Under the Dawes Act, reservations were allotted and the surplus sold, cutting Native land from about 138 to 48 million acres.

questions.prompt: Who investigated lynchings and found their usual excuse was almost always false?

options.label: Ida Tarbell
Jane Addams
Clara Lemlich
Ida B. Wells

questions.explanation: Ida B. Wells investigated lynchings and published Southern Horrors in 1892.

questions.prompt: Level 7 showed horses remaking Plains life around the bison hunt. Which event in this chapter struck at that way of life?

options.label: The Triangle fire
The Great Slaughter of the bison
The opening of Ellis Island
options.rationale: That was an East Coast gateway.

options.label: The breakup of Standard Oil
options.rationale: That was about oil, not the Plains.

questions.explanation: Railways, rifles, the hide trade and the army cut the bison from tens of millions to under 1,000.
